courses.subject: MAEG
courses.title: Prototypes to Products
courses.description: This course covers the fundamental ideas and concepts of product engineering processes from a prototype to product. Students learn about creativity and product engineering principles through both lectures and practical projects. Topics include opportunity identification; idea generation; survey of customers and markets; devising concepts and building models and drawings; building and testing mockups; project management; and construction of a high quality prototype. We encourage students to form teams and enroll together.

courses.subject: MAEG
courses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical and Automation Engineering
courses.description:
Mechanical and automation engineering covers a wide range of topics related to physical machines and mechanisms that involve force and movement. The focus of the course varies according to the area of expertise of the instructor. The instructor will design lectures, tutorials, fieldtrips and/or hands-on activities around special topic(s). Drawing on the background, experiences and interests of the students, the course will consider the topics from mechanics, design, materials, fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, control, mechatronics and robotics.

This course is exclusively designed for Bing Overseas Studies Program (BOSP) of Stanford University.
courses.course_syllabus:
The course may cover various scopes of studies while some suggested areas may include:
(1) Statics and dynamics
(2) Mechanisms design
(3) Mechanics of materials
(4) Fabrication and production
(5) Thermodynamics
(6) Fluid mechanics
(7) Control
(8) Mechatronic systems
(9) Robotics

Up-to-date topics will be delivered every week.

courses.subject: MAEG
courses.title: Microelectromechanical Systems Technology and Applications
courses.description: This course covers the general introduction to the fabrication and design of micro-systems including different fabrication processes of integrated circuits, emerging micro- and nanoscale fabrication processes; as well as modeling and design of microelectromechanical systems (MEMS). Important topics includes scaling law, integrated circuits fabrication processes, modeling and design of microscale sensors and actuators, and the applications of micro-sensors and actuators to form micro-systems for different applications, including automobiles, robotics, biomedical, and aerospace etc.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Mechanical and Automation Engineering;Not for students who have taken ENGG5404
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, students should have achieved the following outcomes:
1. Understand state-of-the-art technologies for fabricating micro- and nano-scale structures, machines, and systems;
2. Understand the principles that govern the designs of micro/nano sensors and actuators; and
3. Apply applications of MEMS and Nanotechnology in advanced research projects and commercial products.

courses.subject: MAEG
courses.title: Railway Engineering and Systems
courses.description: The course is designed to allow the postgraduate students to be kept abreast of the various key engineering systems and processes for a modern railway. This includes key components and core systems of modern railway systems including rolling stock, signaling, communication, control, AFC, traction power systems; and key processes including project management; system integration including system V&V process, project lifecycle modeling, system assurance and EMC management as well as railway development planning. In addition, introduction to new technologies being researched and applied to railway project and operation will also be covered in the course.
